_comment: Coverage map for check-features (docs/testing/feature-coverage.md). Maps each documented requirement unit (FR-N.M / NFR-N.M, or a N.M subsection number for older docs) to the test(s) that would fail if the behavior regressed. Stateful units set stateful:true and list the transitions the tests exercise. This map is intentionally partial; `npm run check:features` reports every unmapped or under-tested unit as a gap. Filling it out is an ongoing exercise (GB-1012); every mapping below is verified against the cited test, and genuine gaps are left unmapped rather than papered over.

3.1.note: isGitRepo (repo check), getRepoRoot (root path), getRepoName (name), getHeadCommit (HEAD SHA) — all four sub-behaviors asserted.

3.2.note: getDiffArgs covers every review mode's git command mapping; parseDiff asserts structured parsing (path/oldPath/status/hunks) + line metadata (type/old/new/content).

3.4.note: Binary detection from git's diff header is asserted (parseDiff 'parses a binary file'; diffRawContent binary). GAP: the untracked-file first-8KB null-byte scan in createNewFileDiff is not separately tested (tied to the 3.3 gap).

transitions: multiple schedule calls within the window -> coalesced into one export (debounce)
debounce window elapses uninterrupted -> export fires once
flush -> pending export fires immediately and the timer is canceled (no double fire)
isCurrent true -> writes latest-review.md + archive; isCurrent false -> archive only

6.2.note: Header, Annotation Summary (per-category counts), Items to Remember, per-file annotations, and AI-tool instructions sections are each asserted.

6.2a.note: buildReviewExportData shape: clean mode label, group-by-comparison, omit no-annotation files, ground-truth context, region denormalization by scope, schemaVersion rejection. Consumed by the --on-complete hook (export paths in env).

6.3.note: Deletion cleanup asserted (deleteReviewExport removes archive; no-op when absent). GAP: reopen-preserves-export is not directly asserted.

6.4.note: Export renders plain markdown grouped by (relative) file path; the AI-instructions section is asserted.

transitions: getDb before setDataDir -> throws
first getDb -> creates PGlite pinned to template1 + runs schema SQL
subsequent getDb -> returns the same instance (singleton)
migration: adds a missing column when absent (idempotent when present)
startup -> running analyses reset to failed

9.2.note: reviews / review_files / annotations CRUD (queries), ai_analyses / ai_file_scores (ai-queries), attachments (store). user_preferences exercised via ai-queries/preferences.

9.3.note: config.json chmod 0600, base64-encoded keys, and GLASSBOX_CONFIG_DIR override all asserted.

9.6.note: Isolation by repo_path (listReviews repoPath filter); instance lock prevents concurrent access (lock.test.ts).

FR-26.1.note: Ground-truth is a distinct mode: groundTruthSideLabels reads it and returns undefined for non-GT modes.

FR-26.4.note: loadGroundTruthManifest resolves actual<->expected pairs relative to the manifest dir (and keeps absolutes).

FR-26.5.note: Single still-image pairs (v1 comparisons[]); images-only enforcement.

FR-26.6.note: comparePerceptual difference score; identical=0, differing dims=1, unsupported/corrupt=undecodable.

FR-26.8.note: Source list reads as named comparisons (groundTruthMetaByFileId maps file id -> label/expectedKind).

FR-26.9.note: A set is an ordered flow: v2 sets resolve to one ordered entry per step with derived keys, in order.

FR-26.10.note: buildGroundTruthSourceList groups set steps as named groups in declared/stepIndex order.

FR-26.11.note: Per-step scores + a max aggregate per set; singles and sets sorted most-different-first.

FR-26.12.note: groundTruthStepNav reports step k of N with bounded prev/next within the set.

FR-26.15.note: Baseline rotation stays external: promote copies actual over previous-actual, never overwrites spec/reference, skips missing, handles v2 sets.

5.1.note: addAnnotation creates with defaults (category, side, timestamps); reply_to_note_id when threading a note reply.

5.4.note: moveAnnotation changes line + side and clears stale (the persistence of drag-and-drop). The DnD UI gesture itself is covered by e2e, not here.

transitions: markAnnotationStale -> markAnnotationCurrent cycle
deleteStaleAnnotations removes only stale rows, leaves current
migration: exact match stays; shifted line follows content; moved outside radius -> stale; content reappears -> unmarked current

5.7.note: Annotations persist across the full CRUD surface (create/read/update/delete/move round-trip through PGLite).

15.1.note: Active theme is read/written (getActiveThemeId/setActiveThemeId), default fallback on missing/corrupt config.

15.2.note: Built-in theme set: count, order, unique ids/names, dark/light background sanity.

15.3.note: Custom themes: loadCustomThemes (skips non-json/corrupt/missing-field), saveCustomTheme, deleteCustomTheme, getCustomTheme.

15.4.note: THEME_VARIABLES set (background/text/diff/gutter); every theme defines all required color variables.

15.8.note: StoredCustomThemeSchema validates the on-disk file format (well-formed / partial colors / rejects empty id-name / non-string colors).

15.9.note: Theme REST API: list / get-set active / create-update-delete custom.

20.1.note: Notes are written to path-mirrored .NNNNNN.sarif shards under .pr-notes/, with shard roll-over at the cap.

20.2.note: SARIF 2.1.0: emptyLog is a valid log with producer as tool.driver.name; buildResult maps anchor/body/snippet/kind/confidence/ticket to standard + namespaced fields.

transitions: snippet still matches its line -> untouched
authored text moved -> re-anchored to the new line
line shown but text gone -> flagged stale
line not in the diff -> untouched (cannot judge)
text appears more than once -> nearest match chosen

20.4.note: glassbox note add/update/remove/coalesce; writeReviewNote appends into the shard, updateNote patches in place, removeNote by guid, coalesce drops redundant.

20.5.note: Artifacts: text artifact read inline, image artifacts marked as , missing/binary surfaced as reference, path-escape refused; SARIF result.attachments mapping. GAP: live diagram rendering (P4 remainder) not yet built/tested.

20.6.note: loadReviewNotesForFile flattens notes to diff-anchored view items on the new side; scoped to the requested file; skips corrupt shards.

20.7.note: reviewNotesExportSection emits a markdown section with per-file notes + producer attribution — what Hot Sheet / other orchestrators consume.

20.8.note: reviewNotesPromptSection folds notes into the analysis prompt; store round-trips notes losslessly.

20.9.note: Interoperability: preserves unknown fields written by another tool on round-trip; refuses to overwrite a non-SARIF shard; groups results into per-producer runs.

FR-25.1.note: Any file type: the store round-trips arbitrary bytes and records size + sha.

FR-25.8.note: Readable by the AI tool: the markdown export lists each attachment's path under its annotation (doc 25).

NFR-25.1.note: Local storage: bytes live on disk under <dataDir>/attachments/, named by id + sanitized original.

NFR-25.3.note: Path containment: sanitizeFilename strips separators + control/reserved chars so a name cannot escape the dir; falls back when it sanitizes away.

FR-27.1.note: ensureGlassboxGitignored runs at launch inside a git repo.

transitions: already-present -> no-op (idempotent re-run)
no trailing newline -> block appended cleanly
FR-27.3.note: Idempotency is a transition, not a single-op check: run twice, second run must not change the file.

transitions: stale bare '.glassbox/' -> replaced with canonical block
stale variants (.glassbox, /.glassbox, /.glassbox/*) -> replaced
multiple stale lines -> collapsed into one block at first position
no file -> created fresh
empty/whitespace file -> block created
commented opt-out present -> file left untouched
any commented .glassbox variant -> treated as opt-out

NFR-27.1.note: computeGitignore is a pure function; the whole suite exercises it without touching disk.

NFR-27.2.note: Unrelated entries containing the word glassbox are left untouched.
